discovery: Development of high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy into a momentum-resolved probe of many-body electronic structure, revealing the d-wave gap, pseudogap and quasiparticle renormalisation in high-temperature superconductors

nominees.name: Zhi-Xun Shen
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Juan Carlos Campuzano
nominees.affiliation: University of Illinois Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

subfield: Experimental condensed matter physics (quantum materials spectroscopy)
motivation: The nominees turned angle-resolved photoemission from a band-mapping tool into a precision probe of interacting electrons in solids. Through advances in energy and momentum resolution and synchrotron instrumentation, they directly imaged the anisotropic d-wave superconducting gap in the cuprates (1993 onward), discovered the normal-state pseudogap and Fermi arcs, and resolved the quasiparticle kinks and self-energies that expose electron-boson coupling. These results, reproduced across materials and confirmed by tunnelling, neutron and phase-sensitive probes, reshaped how physicists understand correlated electrons and unconventional superconductivity. The method they established now underpins discovery across quantum matter: topological insulators and Weyl semimetals, iron-based superconductors, graphene and moiré materials, and femtosecond time-resolved studies of light-driven phases. Few experimental techniques have so broadly opened a new window onto the quantum many-body problem.
